description: We are building a sovereign geospatial telemetry engine to harmonize MODIS and VIIRS active fire data for the NASA challenge. Powered by quantticks.com, our solution ingests real-time spatial feeds, normalizes multi-sensor schemas across global regions, and delivers compressed, analytics-ready datasets for interactive dashboards. We welcome engineers passionate about spatial telemetry and modern enterprise data pipelines.
summary:
Quantticks Oracle is a zero-trust environmental intelligence command center designed to harmonize orbital thermal anomaly detection and Fire Radiative Power (FRP) monitoring across NASA and NOAA satellite constellations (MODIS and VIIRS). Addressing critical needs for multi-sensor transparency, our platform ingests and normalizes active fire telemetry via Cloudflare R2 and DuckDB, achieving an ~80.5% data compression ratio through ZSTD formatting. 

Deployed live at nasa.quantticks.com, Quantticks Oracle features an interactive Hugo and Plotly.js command center with granular judge-requested filters for MODIS Only, VIIRS Only, and Combined views, alongside precise geospatial hotspot mapping, regional breakdowns, and instant CSV export capabilities. By bridging raw orbital satellite data with blazing-fast rendering, our solution empowers emergency responders and researchers with transparent, cross-calibrated global wildfire intelligence.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Quantticks Oracle is a zero-trust environmental intelligence command center that ingests, normalizes, and visualizes global active fire telemetry from NASA and NOAA satellite constellations—specifically MODIS (1 km resolution) and VIIRS (375 m resolution)[cite: 4].

Our backend ingestion pipeline pulls active fire feeds across major global fire-prone regions (including California, Alberta, the Amazon Basin, the Mediterranean, Southeast Australia, Siberia, Indonesia, and Newfoundland & Atlantic Canada)[cite: 4]. It harmonizes disparate sensor schemas—mapping brightness temperatures (brightness and bright_ti4), Fire Radiative Power (FRP), and confidence scores into a unified columnar schema[cite: 4]—and stores the output as ZSTD-compressed Apache Parquet files in Cloudflare R2 object storage (`quantticks-nasa-parquet`). Analytical queries are accelerated via DuckDB, generating lightweight structured JSON payloads rendered by a static Hugo and Plotly.js web application live at https://nasa.quantticks.com.

Key Benefits & Intended Impact

• Cross-Sensor Transparency & Granular Control: Directly addressing feedback during judging review, the dashboard allows researchers and emergency responders to toggle seamlessly between MODIS + VIIRS Combined, MODIS Only, and VIIRS Only modes, isolating sensor-specific detection volumes and regional breakdowns.

• High-Efficiency Storage & Zero-Bloat Delivery: By utilizing ZSTD-compressed Parquet storage paired with static site edge delivery on Cloudflare Pages, the platform eliminates heavy database server overhead while maintaining sub-second global map rendering.

• Actionable Field Exports: Users can filter hotspots by geographic region and confidence thresholds and export customized datasets directly to CSV in the browser[cite: 4].

Tools, Coding Languages & Architecture

• Data Engineering & Storage: Python, DuckDB, Apache Parquet (ZSTD compression), Cloudflare R2 (S3-compatible object storage)[cite: 4]

• Frontend & Visualization: Hugo Static Site Generator, HTML5/CSS3, JavaScript, Plotly.js (interactive ScatterGeo mapping and distribution charts)[cite: 4]

• DevOps & Source Control: GitHub, GitHub Actions CI/CD (.github/workflows/deploy.yml), Cloudflare Pages[cite: 4]

• Public Source Repository: https://github.com/code2expert/quantticks-nasa[cite: 8]

Creativity & Design Considerations

Rather than relying on expensive, high-latency GIS servers that often bottleneck during peak disaster events, we designed Quantticks Oracle around decentralized data sovereignty and deterministic edge caching. Abstracting sensor schemas at the Parquet layer while preserving granular sensor filtering at the UI layer ensures both scientific rigor and immediate usability for disaster preparedness teams, researchers, and local communities.
